controlled_change: Only cache_policy: clock versus slru, in two fresh-process alternating pairs at 12GiB and 1,848 slots. Same mixed artifact, reference kernels, prompt, output limits and sampling.
correctness: 55 native tests and 45,673 assertions with Metal validation; 164 Python tests. Real 32-slot all-layer fixture matched logits, routes and persistent state, continued versus fresh replay, cancellation and failure. Timed conversations generated identical tokens and reuse.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: Fewer expert reads and lower conversation latency at equal memory. This ledger interpretation is retrospective; the two-pair gate was recorded before timing.
hypothesis: A native 75-percent-protected SLRU expert cache can turn the prior simulated read reduction into lower complete coding-request latency.
limitations: Two pairs do not establish confidence or an attributable speedup.
The 32-step short-history workload differs from the prior 256-step locality capture and 4K-history append target.
Compression counters vary, but their totals do not prove a critical-path cause.
Native arithmetic parity is separate from independent model correctness and coding quality.
SLRU remains opt-in for bench/inspect; no production default, precision, model weights or OS settings changed.
outcome: SLRU consistently reduced expert misses from 30,264 to 27,321 (9.72 percent). Whole-conversation ratios were 0.840336 and 1.050781. Follow-up requests were 3.69 and 3.57 percent faster, but overall repeatability failed. Compression activity varied substantially. Complete experiment took 316.14 seconds.
smallest_experiment: Inspect the saved memory and dependency evidence to design one bounded diagnostic for initial-generation timing variance. Keep CLOCK as default; do not start five-pair or full qualification from this failed gate.
